requirements: stream must be a valid OS stream object and currently open for writing.

requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle opened on an archive

functions.name: mz_zip_goto_next_entry
functions.description: Advances to the next entry in the ZIP archive, returning MZ_END_OF_LIST when no more entries are available.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle opened on an archive
Caller must handle the MZ_END_OF_LIST status code to detect end of iteration

functions.name: mz_zip_locate_entry
functions.signature: int32_t mz_zip_locate_entry(void *handle, const char *filename, uint8_t ignore_case)
functions.description: Finds an entry by name in the ZIP file, optionally ignoring case. Returns MZ_END_OF_LIST if not found.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle opened on an archive
filename must be a non-NULL, null-terminated UTF-8 string
ignore_case is a flag controlling case-sensitivity (exact accepted values beyond 0/1 unknown)
Caller must handle MZ_END_OF_LIST when not found

functions.name: mz_zip_locate_first_entry
functions.description: Starts a search for entries matching a user-supplied callback predicate. Positions at the first matching entry.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle opened on an archive
cb must be a non-NULL callback of type mz_zip_locate_entry_cb
userdata is passed through to the callback and may be NULL
Callback is invoked with file info for matching; it must not corrupt the handle or provided structures

functions.name: mz_zip_locate_next_entry
functions.description: Continues searching for the next entry that matches the callback predicate established by locate_first_entry.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle opened on an archive
cb must be a non-NULL callback of type mz_zip_locate_entry_cb
userdata may be NULL
Caller must handle MZ_END_OF_LIST when no further matches are found

functions.name: mz_zip_attrib_is_dir
functions.description: Determines whether the provided file attribute flags represent a directory, taking into account the originating platform (version_madeby).
requirements: attrib must be a valid attribute bitmask for the source platform
version_madeby must indicate the originating host system per ZIP spec (exact values unknown)

functions.name: mz_zip_attrib_is_symlink
functions.description: Determines whether the provided file attribute flags represent a symbolic link, considering the originating platform.
requirements: attrib must be a valid attribute bitmask for the source platform
version_madeby must indicate the originating host system per ZIP spec (exact values unknown)

functions.name: mz_zip_attrib_convert
functions.signature: int32_t mz_zip_attrib_convert(uint8_t src_sys, uint32_t src_attrib, uint8_t target_sys, uint32_t *target_attrib)
functions.description: Converts file attribute bits from one host system representation to another.
requirements: target_attrib must be a non-NULL pointer to receive converted attributes
src_sys and target_sys must be valid host identifiers as used by ZIP (exact mapping values unknown)

functions.name: mz_zip_attrib_posix_to_win32
functions.description: Converts POSIX file mode/attributes to Win32 file attribute flags.
requirements: win32_attrib must be a non-NULL pointer to receive converted attributes

functions.name: mz_zip_attrib_win32_to_posix
functions.description: Converts Win32 file attribute flags to POSIX mode/attributes.
requirements: posix_attrib must be a non-NULL pointer to receive converted attributes

functions.name: mz_zip_extrafield_find
functions.signature: int32_t mz_zip_extrafield_find(void *stream, uint16_t type, int32_t max_seek, uint16_t *length)
functions.description: Seeks within a stream to locate an extra field by its header type and returns the field length.
requirements: stream must be a valid readable/seekable stream positioned at the start of extra fields
type must be the desired extra field header ID
max_seek limits how far to search; must be >= 0
length must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the length on success

functions.name: mz_zip_extrafield_contains
functions.signature: int32_t mz_zip_extrafield_contains(const uint8_t *extrafield, int32_t extrafield_size, uint16_t type, uint16_t *length)
functions.description: Checks a memory buffer of extra fields for the presence of a field with the given type and, if present, returns its size.
requirements: extrafield must point to a buffer of size extrafield_size bytes; if NULL, extrafield_size should be 0 (not explicitly stated; behavior unknown)
extrafield_size must be >= 0
length must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the field length if found

functions.name: mz_zip_extrafield_read
functions.description: Reads an extra field header (type and length) from the given stream.
requirements: stream must be a valid readable stream positioned at an extra field header
type must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the ID
length must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the length

functions.name: mz_zip_extrafield_write
functions.signature: int32_t mz_zip_extrafield_write(void *stream, uint16_t type, uint16_t length)
functions.description: Writes an extra field header (type and length) to the given stream.
requirements: stream must be a valid writable stream positioned where the header should be written
type and length must be valid values per ZIP extra field format

functions.name: mz_zip_dosdate_to_tm
functions.description: Converts a DOS date/time value to a struct tm.
requirements: ptm must be a non-NULL pointer to a struct tm to receive the result
dos_date must be a valid DOS date/time encoding

functions.name: mz_zip_dosdate_to_time_t
functions.description: Converts a DOS date/time value to a time_t (Unix time).
requirements: dos_date must be a valid DOS date/time encoding

functions.name: mz_zip_tm_to_time_t
functions.description: Converts a struct tm to time_t (Unix time).
requirements: ptm must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid struct tm

functions.name: mz_zip_time_t_to_tm
functions.description: Converts a time_t (Unix time) to a struct tm.
requirements: ptm must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the converted time

functions.name: mz_zip_time_t_to_dos_date
functions.description: Converts a time_t (Unix time) to a DOS date/time value.

functions.name: mz_zip_tm_to_dosdate
functions.description: Converts a struct tm to a DOS date/time value.
requirements: ptm must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid struct tm

functions.name: mz_zip_ntfs_to_unix_time
functions.description: Converts an NTFS timestamp to Unix time_t.
requirements: unix_time must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the converted time
ntfs_time must be a valid NTFS timestamp value

functions.name: mz_zip_unix_to_ntfs_time
functions.description: Converts a Unix time_t to an NTFS timestamp.
requirements: ntfs_time must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the converted time

functions.name: mz_zip_path_compare
functions.signature: int32_t mz_zip_path_compare(const char *path1, const char *path2, uint8_t ignore_case)
functions.description: Compares two path strings while ignoring directory separator differences, optionally ignoring case. Returns a comparison result.
requirements: path1 and path2 must be non-NULL, null-terminated strings
ignore_case is a flag controlling case-sensitivity (exact accepted values beyond 0/1 unknown)

functions.name: mz_zip_get_compression_method_string
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string name for a compression method identifier.
requirements: compression_method must be a valid method identifier (exact mapping values unknown)
Returned string is constant and must not be modified by the caller

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_is_open
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the zip reader instance referenced by handle currently has an archive open, zero otherwise.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance created by mz_zip_reader_create() or equivalent
Function is query-only; it does not open the archive

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_open
functions.description: Opens a zip archive for reading from a custom stream object.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance created by mz_zip_reader_create()
stream must be a valid initialized stream compatible with the library (type unspecified here)
Must not already have an archive open on handle before calling
On success, close with mz_zip_reader_close()

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_open_file
functions.description: Opens a zip archive for reading from a filesystem path.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance
path must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string referring to an accessible file
Must not already have an archive open on handle before calling
Close with mz_zip_reader_close()

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_open_file_in_memory
functions.description: Opens a zip archive from a file path and loads it into memory for faster access.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance
path must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated existing file path
Sufficient memory must be available to load the archive
Must not already have an archive open on handle before calling
Close with mz_zip_reader_close()

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_open_buffer
functions.signature: int32_t mz_zip_reader_open_buffer(void *handle, const uint8_t *buf, int32_t len, uint8_t copy);
functions.description: Opens a zip archive for reading directly from a memory buffer.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance
buf must point to at least len bytes of readable memory
len must be >= 0
If copy == 0, the buffer must remain valid and unmodified for the lifetime of the open reader
Must not already have an archive open on handle before calling
Close with mz_zip_reader_close()

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_close
functions.description: Closes the currently open zip archive on the reader.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance
Safe to call only after a successful open
After close, entry iteration/reading functions must not be used until re-opened

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_unzip_cd
functions.description: Extracts (inflates) the central directory if the archive has a zipped central directory, preparing it for entry queries.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance with an archive open
Typically used when the central directory is stored compressed

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_goto_first_entry
functions.description: Positions the reader at the first entry that matches the current pattern settings.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance with an archive open
If a pattern was set via mz_zip_reader_set_pattern(), matching is applied; otherwise all entries are considered

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_goto_next_entry
functions.description: Advances to the next entry matching the current pattern settings.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance with an archive open
Call after mz_zip_reader_goto_first_entry() or a successful locate
Fails when there are no more matching entries

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_locate_entry
functions.signature: int32_t mz_zip_reader_locate_entry(void *handle, const char *filename, uint8_t ignore_case);
functions.description: Searches for an entry by filename and positions the reader on it if found.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance with an archive open
filename must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string
ignore_case controls case-insensitive matching (non-zero to ignore case)

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_entry_open
functions.description: Opens the current entry for reading its data.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance with an archive open
The reader must be positioned on a valid entry via goto/locate functions
Call before mz_zip_reader_entry_read() or entry save functions
Close with mz_zip_reader_entry_close()

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_entry_close
functions.description: Closes the currently open entry.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance
An entry must have been opened with mz_zip_reader_entry_open()
Must be called to finalize reading of the entry before moving to another entry or closing the archive

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_entry_read
functions.description: Reads up to len bytes from the currently open entry into buf.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance
An entry must be opened with mz_zip_reader_entry_open()
buf must be a non-NULL writable buffer of at least len bytes
len must be >= 0
Repeat calls continue reading until EOF or error

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_entry_get_hash
functions.signature: int32_t mz_zip_reader_entry_get_hash(void *handle, uint16_t algorithm, uint8_t *digest, int32_t digest_size);
functions.description: Retrieves the specified hash algorithm's digest from the current entry's extra fields.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance positioned on an entry (open not necessarily required for metadata)
algorithm must specify a supported hash algorithm identifier
digest must point to a writable buffer
digest_size must be >= required size for the specified algorithm

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_entry_get_first_hash
functions.description: Returns the most secure/first available hash algorithm and its digest size from the current entry's extra fields.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance positioned on an entry
algorithm must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the algorithm id
digest_size must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the required size

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_entry_get_info
functions.description: Provides a pointer to the metadata (mz_zip_file) for the current entry.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance positioned on an entry
file_info must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the metadata pointer
The mz_zip_file type definition is external to this header and must be understood by the caller

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_entry_is_dir
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the current entry represents a directory, zero otherwise.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance positioned on an entry

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_entry_save
functions.description: Extracts the current entry and writes it to a destination stream via the provided write callback.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance
An entry must be opened with mz_zip_reader_entry_open()
stream must be a valid destination stream/context understood by write_cb
write_cb must be a valid function pointer that writes data to stream

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_entry_save_process
functions.description: Processes and writes a portion of the current entry to the stream via callback, enabling incremental extraction.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance
An entry must be opened with mz_zip_reader_entry_open()
stream must be valid
write_cb must be a valid function pointer

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_entry_save_file
functions.description: Extracts and saves the current entry to a file at the specified path.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance
An entry must be opened with mz_zip_reader_entry_open()
path must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string indicating the destination path
Caller should ensure filesystem permissions and free space are adequate

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_entry_save_buffer
functions.description: Extracts the current entry into a caller-provided memory buffer of length len.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance
An entry must be opened with mz_zip_reader_entry_open()
buf must be a non-NULL writable buffer
len must be >= the required output size; otherwise the call fails or truncates depending on implementation (not specified)
Use mz_zip_reader_entry_save_buffer_length() to determine required buffer length

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_entry_save_buffer_length
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes required to save the current entry into a memory buffer.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance
Call while positioned on the desired entry; for compressed entries, this typically reflects uncompressed size

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_save_all
functions.description: Extracts all matching entries from the archive to the specified directory.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance with an archive open
destination_dir must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated directory path
Affected by any pattern set via mz_zip_reader_set_pattern()
Caller should ensure destination directory exists or is creatable with proper permissions

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_set_pattern
functions.signature: void mz_zip_reader_set_pattern(void *handle, const char *pattern, uint8_t ignore_case);
functions.description: Sets a filename match pattern for entry enumeration. If pattern is NULL, all entries are matched.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance
pattern may be NULL to match all entries
ignore_case non-zero to ignore case during matching

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_set_password
functions.description: Sets the password to use when extracting encrypted entries.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance
password may be NULL to clear any previously set password; otherwise must be a NUL-terminated string

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_set_raw
functions.description: Controls whether entries should be saved raw (without decompression or transformation).
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance
raw is a boolean-like flag (0/1)

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_get_raw
functions.description: Retrieves whether entries are configured to be saved raw.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance
raw must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the flag

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_get_zip_cd
functions.description: Indicates whether the archive has a zipped (compressed) central directory.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance with an archive open
zip_cd must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the flag

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_get_comment
functions.description: Retrieves the central directory comment string for the archive.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance with an archive open
comment must be a non-NULL pointer to receive a pointer to a NUL-terminated string (lifetime/ownership unspecified)

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_set_recover
functions.description: Enables or disables recovery of the central directory by scanning local file headers.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance
recover is a boolean-like flag (0/1)

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_set_encoding
functions.description: Specifies support for a particular character encoding for file names within the zip archive.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance
encoding must be a value understood by the library (exact constants not specified here)

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_set_overwrite_cb
functions.description: Registers a callback invoked when a file being extracted would overwrite an existing file.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance
cb may be NULL to clear the callback; otherwise must match mz_zip_reader_overwrite_cb signature
userdata is an opaque pointer passed to the callback

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_set_password_cb
functions.description: Registers a callback to supply a password when needed and none has been set.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance
cb may be NULL to clear the callback; otherwise must match mz_zip_reader_password_cb signature
userdata is an opaque pointer passed to the callback

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_set_progress_cb
functions.description: Registers a progress callback for extraction operations.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance
cb may be NULL to clear the callback; otherwise must match mz_zip_reader_progress_cb signature
userdata is an opaque pointer passed to the callback

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_set_progress_interval
functions.description: Sets the minimum interval between invocations of the progress callback.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance
milliseconds is the minimum elapsed time between progress callbacks

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_set_entry_cb
functions.description: Registers a callback invoked for each zip file entry encountered during enumeration or extraction.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance
cb may be NULL to clear the callback; otherwise must match mz_zip_reader_entry_cb signature
userdata is an opaque pointer passed to the callback

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_get_zip_handle
functions.description: Returns the underlying zip instance handle associated with this reader.
requirements: handle must be a valid reader instance
zip_handle must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the internal handle

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_create
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new zip reader instance.
requirements: Caller is responsible for deleting the instance with mz_zip_reader_delete()

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_delete
functions.description: Deletes a zip reader instance and frees associated resources.
requirements: handle must be a non-NULL pointer to a reader handle variable
*handle should be a reader created by mz_zip_reader_create()
After deletion, the handle will no longer be valid

functions.name: mz_zip_writer_is_open
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the zip writer instance currently has an archive open for writing, zero otherwise.
requirements: handle must be a valid writer instance created by mz_zip_writer_create()

functions.name: mz_zip_writer_open
functions.description: Opens a zip archive for writing to a custom stream. If append is non-zero, appends to an existing archive where supported.
requirements: handle must be a valid writer instance
stream must be a valid initialized stream compatible with the library
append is a boolean-like flag (0/1)
Must not already have an archive open on handle before calling
Close with mz_zip_writer_close()

functions.name: mz_zip_writer_open_file
functions.signature: int32_t mz_zip_writer_open_file(void *handle, const char *path, int64_t disk_size, uint8_t append);
functions.description: Opens a zip archive at the given filesystem path for writing. Supports multi-disk/spanning via disk_size and appending to an existing archive when append is non-zero.
requirements: handle must be a valid writer instance
path must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string
disk_size specifies target disk size for spanning; semantics depend on implementation (not fully specified here)
append is a boolean-like flag (0/1)
Must not already have an archive open on handle before calling
Close with mz_zip_writer_close()

functions.name: mz_zip_writer_open_file_in_memory
functions.description: Opens a zip archive from a file path and operates in memory for faster write access.
requirements: handle must be a valid writer instance
path must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string
Sufficient memory must be available
Must not already have an archive open on handle before calling
Close with mz_zip_writer_close()

functions.name: mz_zip_writer_close
functions.description: Closes the zip writer, finalizing the archive.
requirements: handle must be a valid writer instance
Call after a successful open
After close, entry write functions must not be used until re-opened

functions.name: mz_zip_writer_entry_open
functions.description: Opens a new entry in the zip for writing using the provided metadata (filename, attributes, compression settings, etc.).
requirements: handle must be a valid writer instance with an archive open
file_info must point to a properly initialized mz_zip_file describing the entry to create
Close the entry with mz_zip_writer_entry_close()

functions.name: mz_zip_writer_entry_close
functions.description: Closes the currently open entry, finalizing its data and metadata.
requirements: handle must be a valid writer instance
An entry must have been opened with mz_zip_writer_entry_open() before calling

functions.name: mz_zip_writer_entry_write
functions.signature: int32_t mz_zip_writer_entry_write(void *handle, const void *buf, int32_t len);
functions.description: Writes len bytes from buf into the currently open entry.
requirements: handle must be a valid writer instance
An entry must be opened with mz_zip_writer_entry_open()
buf must be a non-NULL readable buffer of at least len bytes
len must be >= 0
May be called repeatedly to stream data into the entry

functions.name: mz_zip_writer_add
functions.description: Writes all available data from the provided stream to the currently open entry using the read callback.
requirements: handle must be a valid writer instance
An entry must be opened with mz_zip_writer_entry_open()
stream must be a valid source stream/context understood by read_cb
read_cb must be a valid function pointer that reads data from stream

functions.name: mz_zip_writer_add_process
functions.description: Processes and writes a portion of data from the source stream to the currently open entry, enabling incremental addition.
requirements: handle must be a valid writer instance
An entry must be opened with mz_zip_writer_entry_open()
stream must be valid
read_cb must be a valid function pointer

functions.name: mz_zip_writer_add_info
functions.signature: int32_t mz_zip_writer_add_info(void *handle, void *stream, mz_stream_read_cb read_cb, mz_zip_file *file_info);
functions.description: Adds an entry to the zip using a source stream and explicit file metadata.
requirements: handle must be a valid writer instance with an archive open
stream must be a valid source stream/context
read_cb must be a valid function pointer
file_info must point to an initialized mz_zip_file structure describing the entry

functions.name: mz_zip_writer_add_buffer
functions.signature: int32_t mz_zip_writer_add_buffer(void *handle, const void *buf, int32_t len, mz_zip_file *file_info);
functions.description: Adds an entry to the zip using data from a memory buffer and the provided metadata.
requirements: handle must be a valid writer instance with an archive open
buf must be a non-NULL readable buffer of at least len bytes
len must be >= 0
file_info must point to an initialized mz_zip_file structure

functions.name: mz_zip_writer_add_file
functions.signature: int32_t mz_zip_writer_add_file(void *handle, const char *path, const char *filename_in_zip);
functions.description: Adds a file from the filesystem into the zip archive under the specified name.
requirements: handle must be a valid writer instance with an archive open
path must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string referring to an existing readable file
filename_in_zip must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string for the entry name

functions.name: mz_zip_writer_add_path
functions.signature: int32_t mz_zip_writer_add_path(void *handle, const char *path, const char *root_path, uint8_t include_path, uint8_t recursive);
functions.description: Enumerates a directory or wildcard path and adds matching entries to the zip. Can include path components and recurse into subdirectories.
requirements: handle must be a valid writer instance with an archive open
path must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string (directory or pattern)
root_path may be NULL or a base path to strip/preserve relative names
include_path is a boolean-like flag controlling path inclusion
recursive is a boolean-like flag to add subdirectories recursively

functions.name: mz_zip_writer_copy_from_reader
functions.description: Copies the current entry from another zip reader instance into this writer, preserving attributes where possible.
requirements: handle must be a valid writer instance with an archive open
reader must be a valid reader instance positioned on an entry to copy

functions.name: mz_zip_writer_set_password
functions.description: Sets the password used for encrypting files added to the zip.
requirements: handle must be a valid writer instance
password may be NULL to clear; otherwise must be a NUL-terminated string

functions.name: mz_zip_writer_set_comment
functions.description: Sets the archive-level comment string.
requirements: handle must be a valid writer instance
comment may be NULL to clear; otherwise must be a NUL-terminated string

functions.name: mz_zip_writer_set_raw
functions.description: Controls whether the writer should write entries in raw form (pre-compressed/pre-encrypted) rather than processing data.
requirements: handle must be a valid writer instance
raw is a boolean-like flag (0/1)

functions.name: mz_zip_writer_get_raw
functions.description: Retrieves whether entries are configured to be written in raw form.
requirements: handle must be a valid writer instance
raw must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the flag

functions.name: mz_zip_writer_set_aes
functions.description: Enables or disables AES encryption for files added to the zip.
requirements: handle must be a valid writer instance
aes is a boolean-like flag (0/1)
Actual AES availability depends on build configuration

functions.name: mz_zip_writer_set_compress_method
functions.description: Sets the compression method used when adding files (e.g., store, deflate).
requirements: handle must be a valid writer instance
compress_method must be a method supported by the library (exact values not specified here)

functions.name: mz_zip_writer_set_compress_level
functions.description: Sets the compression level used when adding files.
requirements: handle must be a valid writer instance
compress_level must be a level supported by the library (exact range not specified here)

functions.name: mz_zip_writer_set_follow_links
functions.description: Controls whether symbolic links are followed when adding files/directories.
requirements: handle must be a valid writer instance
follow_links is a boolean-like flag (0/1)

functions.name: mz_zip_writer_get_follow_links
functions.description: Retrieves the current setting for following symbolic links during path enumeration.
requirements: handle must be a valid writer instance
follow_links must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the flag

functions.name: mz_zip_writer_set_store_links
functions.description: Controls whether symbolic links are stored as links in the zip file rather than dereferenced.
requirements: handle must be a valid writer instance
store_links is a boolean-like flag (0/1)

functions.name: mz_zip_writer_set_zip_cd
functions.description: Controls whether the central directory should be zipped (compressed).
requirements: handle must be a valid writer instance
zip_cd is a boolean-like flag (0/1)

import os
import random
from typing import List

# Data type: arbitrary binary data
# Used by many stubs via FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME. We must return a bytes buffer
# that the harness will use as a shared source for these parameters. Our goal is to craft
# valid, interesting buffers that exercise different code paths while remaining valid as
# generic byte sequences. We will build a container with multiple segments so that different
# consumers slicing from the shared buffer can obtain diverse patterns: ASCII text, UTF-8,
# paths/filenames, ZIP-like signatures, repetitive patterns for find/search, and random data.
#
# Format of produced buffer (no strict parser expected by fuzzer; it's just arbitrary data):
# [Segment table header][segments...]
# Header: b"MZGF" magic + 1 byte segment count + 1 byte reserved + 2-byte total segments length (little-endian)
# Segments: concatenation of sub-buffers in the following order:
#  - ascii_text: mix of words, slashes, wildcards
#  - utf8_text: unicode-rich UTF-8
#  - path_block: platform-like paths (both / and \\), with and without trailing slashes
#  - zip_like: bytes starting with PK\x03\x04 plus some plausible local header fields and filename
#  - pattern_repeats: repeated short patterns to help stream_find
#  - random_block: high-entropy bytes
#  - zeros_block: zero bytes to test size=0/zeroed content behaviors
#  - extrafield_block: plausible ZIP extra field (type,length,data)
#  - small_numbers_block: little-endian integers to feed into read_uint* paths
#
# The buffer remains under 4096 bytes. Lengths are randomized with the seed to provide variety.

ASCII_WORDS = [
    b"hello", b"world", b"test", b"minizip", b"zip", b"entry", b"data",
    b"crc32", b"aes", b"hmac", b"sha", b"buffer", b"stream", b"path",
    b"find", b"reverse", b"write", b"read", b"open", b"close", b"extra",
]

PATH_COMPONENTS = [
    b"src", b"bin", b"tmp", b"var", b"home", b"user", b"docs", b"Downloads",
    b"Pictures", b"Music", b"project", b"build", b"include", b"lib", b"..", b".",
]

FILENAMES = [
    b"file.txt", b"archive.zip", b"image.png", b"README.md", b"Makefile", b"notes.TXT",
    b"script.sh", b"main.c", b"data.bin", b"unicode-", b"path@wild*?.txt",
]

UNICODE_SNIPPETS = [
    "こんにちは", "Привет", "안녕하세요", "مرحبا", "γειά", "héllö", "naïve", "façade",
    "résumé", "São Paulo", "東京", "München", "Κρήτη", "😊🚀📦", "文件", "フォルダ",
]

WILDCARDS = [b"*", b"?", b"**", b"*.zip", b"file.*", b"data??.bin"]


def _rand_choice(r: random.Random, items: List[bytes], k: int) -> List[bytes]:
    return [items[r.randrange(len(items))] for _ in range(k)]


def _ascii_text(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    parts = []
    count = r.randint(10, 40)
    for _ in range(count):
        choice = r.random()
        if choice < 0.6:
            parts.append(r.choice(ASCII_WORDS))
        elif choice < 0.8:
            parts.append(r.choice(WILDCARDS))
        else:
            parts.append(b"/")
    blob = b" ".join(parts)
    return blob[:max_len]


def _utf8_text(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Concatenate several unicode snippets separated by spaces and slashes
    count = r.randint(5, 15)
    seq = []
    for _ in range(count):
        s = r.choice(UNICODE_SNIPPETS)
        # Occasionally add a path-like separator
        if r.random() < 0.3:
            s = s + "/" + r.choice(UNICODE_SNIPPETS)
        seq.append(s)
    txt = " ".join(seq)
    data = txt.encode("utf-8", errors="strict")
    return data[:max_len]


def _path_block(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Generate a mix of Unix and Windows-like paths
    paths = []
    n = r.randint(5, 20)
    for _ in range(n):
        is_win = r.random() < 0.5
        sep = b"\\" if is_win else b"/"
        depth = r.randint(1, 5)
        comps = _rand_choice(r, PATH_COMPONENTS, depth)
        # Optionally append a filename
        if r.random() < 0.7:
            comps.append(r.choice(FILENAMES))
        p = sep.join(comps)
        # Sometimes trailing slash
        if r.random() < 0.3:
            p += sep
        paths.append(p)
    joined = b"\n".join(paths)
    return joined[:max_len]


def _zip_like(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Minimal PK local file header-ish sequence: PK\x03\x04 + fields + filename + extra
    # Not necessarily valid ZIP, but structurally suggestive and safe as arbitrary bytes.
    def le16(x):
        return (x & 0xFFFF).to_bytes(2, "little")
    def le32(x):
        return (x & 0xFFFFFFFF).to_bytes(4, "little")

    sig = b"PK\x03\x04"
    ver = le16(r.choice([20, 45, 63]))
    flags = le16(r.randrange(0, 1 << 11))
    method = le16(r.choice([0, 8, 99]))  # store, deflate, AES placeholder
    time = le16(r.randrange(0, 0xFFFF))
    date = le16(r.randrange(0, 0xFFFF))
    crc32 = le32(r.getrandbits(32))
    csz = le32(r.randrange(0, 4096))
    usz = le32(r.randrange(0, 4096))
    fname = r.choice(FILENAMES)
    # Add random unicode suffix occasionally
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        fname += ("-" + r.choice(UNICODE_SNIPPETS)).encode("utf-8")
    extra_len = r.randrange(0, 64)
    hdr = sig + ver + flags + method + time + date + crc32 + csz + usz + le16(len(fname)) + le16(extra_len)
    extra = os.urandom(extra_len) if extra_len else b""
    body = fname + extra
    blob = hdr + body
    return blob[:max_len]


def _pattern_repeats(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Choose small patterns and repeat them to help find/find_reverse paths
    patterns = [b"A", b"AB", b"ABC", b"\x00\xFF", b"zip", b"CRC", b"GCM", b"SHA", b"HMAC"]
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) < max_len:
        pat = r.choice(patterns)
        reps = r.randint(1, 64)
        out.extend(pat * reps)
        # Insert separators sometimes
        if r.random() < 0.2:
            out.extend(b"\n")
        if len(out) > max_len:
            break
    return bytes(out[:max_len])


def _random_block(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    size = r.randint(max_len // 4, max_len)
    return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(size))


def _zeros_block(max_len: int) -> bytes:
    return b"\x00" * max_len


def _extrafield_block(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Compose several TLV-style fields: [type(2)][len(2)][data]
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) + 4 < max_len:
        t = r.choice([0x0001, 0x5455, 0x7075, 0x9901, r.randrange(0, 0xFFFF)])
        l = r.randrange(0, min(64, max_len - len(out) - 4))
        out.extend((t & 0xFFFF).to_bytes(2, "little"))
        out.extend((l & 0xFFFF).to_bytes(2, "little"))
        if l:
            out.extend(os.urandom(l))
    return bytes(out[:max_len])


def _small_numbers_block(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Sequence of uint8, uint16, uint32, int64, uint64 in little-endian loops
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) + 8 <= max_len:
        out.append(r.randrange(0, 256))  # uint8
        out.extend(r.randrange(0, 65536).to_bytes(2, "little"))  # uint16
        out.extend(r.getrandbits(32).to_bytes(4, "little"))  # uint32
        # Alternate signed/unsigned 64-bit
        out.extend((r.getrandbits(64)).to_bytes(8, "little"))
        if len(out) > max_len:
            break
    return bytes(out[:max_len])


def _build_segments(r: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    # Size budget per segment with overall cap
    total_cap = 3500  # leave room for header and some slack under 4096
    segs = []
    # Determine sizes with some randomness but bounded
    sizes = {
        "ascii": r.randint(200, 500),
        "utf8": r.randint(200, 600),
        "paths": r.randint(200, 700),
        "zip": r.randint(64, 256),
        "repeat": r.randint(128, 512),
        "rand": r.randint(256, 800),
        "zeros": r.randint(64, 256),
        "extra": r.randint(64, 256),
        "nums": r.randint(128, 512),
    }
    # Normalize if exceeding total_cap
    order = ["ascii", "utf8", "paths", "zip", "repeat", "rand", "zeros", "extra", "nums"]
    sum_sizes = sum(sizes[k] for k in order)
    if sum_sizes > total_cap:
        scale = total_cap / float(sum_sizes)
        for k in order:
            sizes[k] = max(32, int(sizes[k] * scale))

    segs.append(_ascii_text(r, sizes["ascii"]))
    segs.append(_utf8_text(r, sizes["utf8"]))
    segs.append(_path_block(r, sizes["paths"]))
    segs.append(_zip_like(r, sizes["zip"]))
    segs.append(_pattern_repeats(r, sizes["repeat"]))
    segs.append(_random_block(r, sizes["rand"]))
    segs.append(_zeros_block(sizes["zeros"]))
    segs.append(_extrafield_block(r, sizes["extra"]))
    segs.append(_small_numbers_block(r, sizes["nums"]))
    return segs


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    segs = _build_segments(r)

    # Header: magic + count + reserved + total length of segments (16-bit, little-endian, modulo 65535)
    magic = b"MZGF"
    count = len(segs)
    payload = b"".join(segs)
    total_len = len(payload) & 0xFFFF
    header = magic + bytes([count & 0xFF]) + b"\x00" + total_len.to_bytes(2, "little")

    out = header + payload
    # Ensure cap <= 4096
    return out[:4096]

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: filesystem path string
# We generate a single bytes buffer that the fuzzer runtime will use to seed
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME. We therefore pack multiple
# interesting NUL-terminated path strings into one buffer, separated by NULs,
# plus some filename-like entries that should exist inside the sandbox when
# FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME is requested. Since we cannot perform I/O, we only
# produce strings; the harness will create the files as needed.
#
# Goals:
# - Cover absolute and relative paths
# - Include different separators ('/' and '\\')
# - Include trailing slash/no trailing slash cases
# - Include dot and dot-dot components
# - Include long names and short names
# - Include edge characters: spaces, unicode-ish (UTF-8), wildcard chars
# - Include extensions and no extensions
# - Include drive letters (Windows-like)
# - Include leading/trailing spaces
# - Include repeated separators and mixed separators
# - Include symlink-like names and hidden files
# - Include directory names likely to be creatable in sandbox
# - Ensure each string is NUL-terminated
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes

_MAX_TOTAL = 4096

def _rand_choice(rnd: random.Random, items: List[str]) -> str:
    return items[rnd.randrange(len(items))]

def _rand_components(rnd: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Generate path components with varied characters (avoid NUL and path separators inside)
    specials = ["-", "_", "+", "=", "@", "#", "$", "%", "^", "()", "[]", "{}", ",", ";", "'", "!", "~"]
    comps = []
    n = rnd.randint(1, 6)
    for _ in range(n):
        kind = rnd.randint(0, 7)
        if kind == 0:
            comps.append(".")
        elif kind == 1:
            comps.append("..")
        elif kind == 2:
            name = ''.join(rnd.choices(string.ascii_letters + string.digits, k=rnd.randint(1, 8)))
            comps.append(name)
        elif kind == 3:
            # include spaces
            name = " ".join([''.join(rnd.choices(string.ascii_lowercase, k=rnd.randint(1, 3))) for _ in range(rnd.randint(1, 3))])
            comps.append(name)
        elif kind == 4:
            # unicode-ish bytes (UTF-8 sequences)
            uni = _rand_choice(rnd, ["café", "東京", "россия", "μZip", "данные", "数据", "árvíztűrő"]) 
            comps.append(uni)
        elif kind == 5:
            # hidden-like
            comps.append("." + ''.join(rnd.choices(string.ascii_lowercase, k=rnd.randint(1, 6))))
        elif kind == 6:
            # long component
            base = ''.join(rnd.choices(string.ascii_letters + string.digits, k=rnd.randint(8, 20)))
            comps.append(base)
        else:
            comps.append(''.join(rnd.choices(string.ascii_letters + string.digits, k=rnd.randint(1, 4))) + _rand_choice(rnd, specials))
    return comps

def _make_path(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    sep = '/' if rnd.randrange(2) == 0 else '\\'
    absolute_styles = [
        sep,                        # Unix-like absolute
        f"C:{sep}",                 # Windows drive absolute
        f"D:{sep}",
        f"//server{sep}share{sep}", # UNC-ish
        ""                          # relative
    ]
    prefix = _rand_choice(rnd, absolute_styles)

    comps = _rand_components(rnd)

    # maybe insert duplicate separators
    parts = []
    for c in comps:
        parts.append(c)
        if rnd.random() < 0.2:
            parts.append("")  # leads to doubled separators when joined

    path = prefix + sep.join(parts)

    # maybe mix separators
    if rnd.random() < 0.3:
        path = path.replace(sep, '/' if sep == '\\' else '\\')

    # maybe add extension
    if rnd.random() < 0.6 and not path.endswith(sep):
        ext = _rand_choice(rnd, [".txt", ".bin", ".zip", ".dat", ".log", ".😀"]) 
        if not any(path.endswith(e) for e in [".txt", ".bin", ".zip", ".dat", ".log", ".😀"]):
            path += ext

    # maybe add trailing slash
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        if not path.endswith(sep):
            path += sep

    # maybe add leading/trailing spaces
    if rnd.random() < 0.2:
        path = (" " * rnd.randint(1, 2)) + path
    if rnd.random() < 0.2:
        path = path + (" " * rnd.randint(1, 2))

    # ensure non-empty
    if path == "":
        path = "."
    return path

def _interesting_fixed_paths() -> List[str]:
    return [
        "/", "/.", "/..", "/tmp/", "/var/log/syslog", "./", "../", ".hidden", ".hidden/",
        "C:/", "C:/Windows/", "C:/Program Files/", "C:\\", "C:\\Temp\\",
        "//server/share/dir/", "//server/share/file.txt",
        "a", "a/", "a/b", "a/b/", "a/b/../c", "a/./b", "a//b///c",
        "path/with space/file name.txt", "path\\with\\mixed/seps/",
        "archive.zip", "nested/dir/archive.zip", "dir/",
        "symlink.lnk", "target.file", "dir.with.dot/", "trailingdot.",
        "name.with.many.dots.tar.gz", "--", "-", "_", "",
    ]

def _dedupe_keep_order(items: List[str]) -> List[str]:
    seen = set()
    out = []
    for s in items:
        if s not in seen:
            seen.add(s)
            out.append(s)
    return out

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # Build a pool of paths
    paths: List[str] = []
    paths.extend(_interesting_fixed_paths())

    # Add a batch of random paths
    for _ in range(40):
        paths.append(_make_path(rnd))

    # Add a few that look like directories derived from a plausible filename base the harness might create
    # Note: FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME returns a real, runtime-created file path; we can't know it here.
    # We still include generic names that the harness can use as derived targets (e.g., adding suffixes .d, .ren, .lnk)
    extra_suffixes = [".d", ".ren", ".lnk"]
    for base in ["fileA.bin", "existing.dat", "sample.txt", "ßeta.bin", "数据.bin"]:
        for suf in extra_suffixes:
            paths.append(base + suf)

    # Add wildcard patterns for mz_path_compare_wc
    wildcards = [
        "*.txt", "file?.bin", "**/logs/*.log", "[a-z]*.dat", "*", "?.*", "*.*", "*zip*",
    ]
    paths.extend(wildcards)

    # Deduplicate and ensure NUL termination per string in final blob
    paths = _dedupe_keep_order(paths)

    # Construct the final buffer as series of C-strings (NUL-terminated)
    blob_parts: List[bytes] = []
    total = 0

    for p in paths:
        # Encode as UTF-8, replace unencodable chars conservatively
        b = p.encode('utf-8', errors='surrogatepass') + b"\x00"
        if total + len(b) > _MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        blob_parts.append(b)
        total += len(b)

    # Ensure at least one entry present
    if not blob_parts:
        blob_parts.append(b".\x00")

    return b"".join(blob_parts)

# Data type: wildcard pattern string
# Target stubs use two places:
# - mz_path_compare_wc(path, wildcard, ignore_case): needs two valid C strings
# - mz_zip_reader_set_pattern(handle, pattern, ignore_case): pattern may be NULL, but FUZZ_PARAM_STR will always provide a buffer; engine may choose NULL itself.
# Our job: return a bytes buffer that the harness splits into FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FILENAME etc.
# We therefore pack multiple interesting strings separated by NULs so each FUZZ_PARAM_STR can pick one slice.
# Strategy: produce a corpus blob consisting of several NUL-terminated strings:
# 1) Realistic file/path samples (Unix/Windows styles)
# 2) Wildcard-heavy patterns exercising '*', '**', '?', character classes, escaped specials, edge cases
# 3) Mixed case paths to exercise ignore_case flag behavior
# 4) Empty strings and single dot/dotdot
# 5) Long path segments near typical limits
# All concatenated with NUL terminators, with a final NUL to ensure last is terminated.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

UNIX_DIRS = ["/", "/home/user", "/var/log", "/tmp", "/a/b/c", "/usr/local/bin"]
WIN_DIRS = [r"C:\\", r"C:\\Users\\User", r"C:\\Temp", r"D:\\data", r"\\\\server\\share"]
FILENAMES = [
    "file.txt", "Makefile", "README.md", "photo.JPG", "archive.zip", "data_001.bin",
    "script.sh", "a", "b.c", ".hidden", "..dot", "longfilenamewithmanycharacters.log",
]

WILDCARDS_BASE = [
    "*", "?", "**", "*.txt", "?.txt", "file.*", "data_??.bin", "*.*", "*.{c,h}",
    "[a-z]*.md", "[!a]*", "{foo,bar,baz}/*", "**/*.c", "**/test?/*", "*.JPG", "photo.*g",
    "*/", "**/", "*/sub/*", "*/sub/**", "????", "*name*", "*.*.*", "*.???",
]

EDGE_PATTERNS = [
    "", ".", "..", "./*", "../*", "**/../*", r"C:\\**\\*.txt", r"?*", r"*?",
    r"[\[\]?*]", # character class-like literal test
]

SLASH_VARIANTS = ["/", "\\"]

# Build long components near common limits

def make_long_name(seed: int, length: int) -> str:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-"
    return ''.join(rnd.choices(chars, k=length))


def random_choice(rnd: random.Random, seq: List[str]) -> str:
    return seq[rnd.randrange(len(seq))]


def build_paths(rnd: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    out = []
    # Plain filenames
    out.extend(FILENAMES)
    # Unix paths
    for d in UNIX_DIRS:
        out.append(d)
        out.extend([f"{d}/{fn}" for fn in FILENAMES])
    # Windows paths
    for d in WIN_DIRS:
        out.append(d)
        out.extend([d + ("\\" if not d.endswith("\\") else "") + fn for fn in FILENAMES])
    # Mixed separators
    out.append("/mixed/sep\\path/file.txt")
    out.append(r"C:\\mixed/sep\\dir/file.TXT")
    # Case variants
    out.append("ReadMe.Md")
    out.append("readme.md")
    # Long near limits
    out.append("/" + make_long_name(rnd.randrange(1<<30), 100) + ".txt")
    out.append(r"C:\\" + make_long_name(rnd.randrange(1<<30), 80) + ".BIN")
    return out


def build_wildcards(rnd: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    out = []
    out.extend(WILDCARDS_BASE)
    out.extend(EDGE_PATTERNS)
    # Combine directories with wildcards
    for base in UNIX_DIRS[:3] + WIN_DIRS[:3]:
        wc = random_choice(rnd, WILDCARDS_BASE)
        slash = random_choice(rnd, SLASH_VARIANTS)
        # Ensure exactly one separator between
        if base and not base.endswith(slash):
            combined = base + slash + wc
        else:
            combined = base + wc
        out.append(combined)
    # Deep recursive patterns
    out.append("**/*.*")
    out.append("**/*.?*")
    # Character classes and ext glob-like sets
    out.append("[a-zA-Z]*/[0-9][0-9]*.log")
    out.append("{src,lib,include}/**/*.[ch]")
    # Escaped specials represented literally for some implementations
    out.append(r"\*.txt")
    out.append(r"\?file")
    # Long wildcard
    longstem = make_long_name(rnd.randrange(1<<30), 64)
    out.append(f"{longstem[:8]}*{longstem[8:16]}?.*")
    return out


def unique_preserve(seq: List[str]) -> List[str]:
    seen = set()
    out = []
    for s in seq:
        if s not in seen:
            seen.add(s)
            out.append(s)
    return out


def pack_cstrings(strings: List[str], max_total: int) -> bytes:
    blob = bytearray()
    for s in strings:
        b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore') + b"\x00"
        if len(blob) + len(b) > max_total:
            break
        blob += b
    if not blob or blob[-1] != 0:
        blob += b"\x00"
    return bytes(blob)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    # Build lists
    paths = build_paths(rnd)
    wcs = build_wildcards(rnd)

    # Shuffle and interleave to provide variety for consecutive FUZZ_PARAM_STR pulls
    rnd.shuffle(paths)
    rnd.shuffle(wcs)

    # Include some duplicates and case toggles to exercise ignore_case
    def toggle_case(s: str) -> str:
        return ''.join(ch.swapcase() if ch.isalpha() and rnd.random() < 0.5 else ch for ch in s)

    extra = []
    for s in paths[:10]:
        extra.append(toggle_case(s))
    for s in wcs[:10]:
        extra.append(toggle_case(s))

    # Always include empty string and single NUL-only entry for robustness
    corpus = [""]
    corpus += unique_preserve(paths[:50] + wcs[:50] + extra)

    # Ensure some particularly interesting combinations at the front
    front = [
        "*.txt",
        "**/*.c",
        "file.txt",
        "/var/log/syslog",
        r"C:\\Temp\\*.JPG",
        "[a-z]*.md",
        "*.*",
        "README.md",
        "",
    ]

    # Prepend front set while preserving uniqueness
    corpus = unique_preserve(front + corpus)

    return pack_cstrings(corpus, MAX_TOTAL)

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Data type: arbitrary binary file contents
# Fuzzer stubs here consume filenames created by the runtime. Our job is to
# provide initial file contents via a single bytes buffer. The runtime will
# place this buffer into a file and pass its path to the target functions.
#
# Targets exercise:
# - mz_file_get_crc: computing CRC32 over file content
# - mz_os_* file attribute and symlink operations: require valid paths; content irrelevant
# - mz_stream_* open calls that may read from the file: prefer a variety of sizes/patterns
# - mz_zip_reader_open_file(_in_memory): expects a valid .zip file to reach deep code paths
# - mz_zip_writer_open_file and add_file: writer uses file path and may read from it when adding
#
# Strategy:
# Generate a mixture of interesting valid contents:
# 1) Small edge cases: empty, 1 byte, tiny random
# 2) Structured patterns: all-zeros, all-0xFF, incrementing, repeating blocks
# 3) Sizes around common boundaries: 512, 1024, 4096, 4095, 4097 (capped to 4096 per requirement)
# 4) A minimal valid ZIP archive so reader_open_file can succeed and enable more code coverage.
#    We'll build a minimal ZIP with one stored (no compression) file and consistent headers.
#
# The generator selects one of these cases deterministically from the seed to
# give diverse and valid inputs.

MAX_OUT = 4096


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _pattern_incrementing(n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes((i % 256) for i in range(n))


def _pattern_repeat(block: bytes, n: int) -> bytes:
    if not block:
        return b""
    repeats = (n + len(block) - 1) // len(block)
    return (block * repeats)[:n]


# ZIP building helpers (PKZip spec minimal):
# Local File Header (LFH):
#  signature: 0x04034b50 (4)
#  version needed: 20 (2)
#  general purpose bit flag: 0 (2)
#  compression method: 0=store (2)
#  file mod time: 0 (2)
#  file mod date: 0 (2)
#  crc-32: crc (4)
#  compressed size: cs (4)
#  uncompressed size: us (4)
#  file name length: nlen (2)
#  extra length: xlen (2)
#  file name bytes
#  extra bytes
#  file data (store)
# Central Directory File Header (CDFH):
#  signature: 0x02014b50 (4)
#  version made by: 20 (2)
#  version needed: 20 (2)
#  flags: 0 (2)
#  method: 0 (2)
#  time:0 (2) date:0 (2)
#  crc: (4)
#  comp size: (4)
#  uncomp size: (4)
#  name len: (2)
#  extra len: (2)
#  comment len: (2) = 0
#  disk number start: (2) = 0
#  internal attr: (2) = 0
#  external attr: (4) = 0
#  relative offset of LFH: (4)
#  name bytes
# End of Central Directory (EOCD):
#  signature: 0x06054b50 (4)
#  disk no:0 (2)
#  disk with cd:0 (2)
#  total entries on this disk:1 (2)
#  total entries:1 (2)
#  cd size: (4)
#  cd offset: (4)
#  comment len:0 (2)


def _crc32_python(data: bytes) -> int:
    # Use zlib.crc32 if available; keep within stdlib without extra deps.
    import zlib
    return zlib.crc32(data) & 0xFFFFFFFF


def _build_minimal_zip(file_name: str, file_data: bytes) -> bytes:
    name_bytes = file_name.encode('utf-8')
    nlen = len(name_bytes)
    xlen = 0
    crc = _crc32_python(file_data)
    comp = file_data  # store method
    cs = len(comp)
    us = len(file_data)

    # Local file header
    lfh = struct.pack('<IHHHHHIIIHH',
                      0x04034B50,  # signature
                      20,          # version needed
                      0,           # flags
                      0,           # method store
                      0, 0,        # time, date
                      crc,
                      cs,
                      us,
                      nlen,
                      xlen)
    lfh_full = lfh + name_bytes + comp

    # Central directory header
    rel_offset = 0  # starts at beginning
    cdfh = struct.pack('<IHHHHHHIIIHHHHHII',
                       0x02014B50,  # signature
                       20,          # version made by
                       20,          # version needed
                       0,           # flags
                       0,           # method
                       0, 0,        # time, date
                       crc,
                       cs,
                       us,
                       nlen,
                       0,           # extra len
                       0,           # comment len
                       0,           # disk number start
                       0,           # internal attr
                       0,           # external attr
                       rel_offset)
    cd = cdfh + name_bytes

    # EOCD
    cd_size = len(cd)
    cd_offset = len(lfh_full)
    eocd = struct.pack('<IHHHHIIH',
                       0x06054B50,
                       0,  # disk no
                       0,  # disk with cd
                       1,  # total entries disk
                       1,  # total entries
                       cd_size,
                       cd_offset,
                       0)  # comment len

    return lfh_full + cd + eocd


def _make_min_zip_case(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Keep file data modest so whole zip < MAX_OUT
    inner_sizes = [0, 1, 7, 32, 123, 512]
    usz = rng.choice(inner_sizes)
    inner = _pattern_repeat(b"ABCDEF\x00\xFF", usz)
    # Ensure deterministic variety
    if usz and rng.random() < 0.5:
        # Mix in some random tail
        tail = _rand_bytes(rng, min(8, usz))
        inner = (inner[:-len(tail)] + tail) if len(inner) >= len(tail) else tail
    name_choices = [
        'file.txt', 'a', 'nested/path.txt', 'unicodé.txt', 'null.bin',
        'dir/empty', 'data', 'x'
    ]
    fname = rng.choice(name_choices)
    zip_bytes = _build_minimal_zip(fname, inner)
    if len(zip_bytes) > MAX_OUT:
        # fallback: shrink inner
        inner = inner[:32]
        zip_bytes = _build_minimal_zip(fname, inner)
    return zip_bytes


def _make_edge_case(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    kinds: List[str] = [
        'empty', 'one_zero', 'one_ff', 'tiny_rand', 'zeros', 'ffs',
        'increment', 'repeat_aa55', 'repeat_text', 'boundary_low', 'boundary_high'
    ]
    k = rng.choice(kinds)
    if k == 'empty':
        return b''
    if k == 'one_zero':
        return b'\x00'
    if k == 'one_ff':
        return b'\xFF'
    if k == 'tiny_rand':
        n = rng.randint(2, 16)
        return _rand_bytes(rng, n)
    if k == 'zeros':
        n = rng.choice([32, 128, 511, 512, 1024])
        return b"\x00" * n
    if k == 'ffs':
        n = rng.choice([33, 129, 255, 513, 1023])
        return b"\xFF" * n
    if k == 'increment':
        n = rng.choice([64, 257, 1024])
        return _pattern_incrementing(n)
    if k == 'repeat_aa55':
        n = rng.choice([128, 300, 4096])
        return _pattern_repeat(b"\xAA\x55", min(n, MAX_OUT))
    if k == 'repeat_text':
        block = b"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.\n"
        n = rng.choice([100, 800, 2048])
        return _pattern_repeat(block, n)
    if k == 'boundary_low':
        n = rng.choice([509, 510, 511, 512, 513])
        return _rand_bytes(rng, n)
    if k == 'boundary_high':
        n = rng.choice([2047, 2048, 2049, 4095, 4096])
        return _rand_bytes(rng, min(n, MAX_OUT))
    return b''


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a scenario with weighted preference for valid ZIP to engage zip readers.
    scenarios = [
        ('zip', 0.45),
        ('edge', 0.35),
        ('random_bulk', 0.20),
    ]
    x = rng.random()
    acc = 0.0
    choice = 'edge'
    for name, w in scenarios:
        acc += w
        if x <= acc:
            choice = name
            break

    if choice == 'zip':
        return _make_min_zip_case(rng)
    elif choice == 'edge':
        return _make_edge_case(rng)
    else:
        # random_bulk: random size up to MAX_OUT with mixed patterns
        total = rng.randint(0, MAX_OUT)
        out = bytearray()
        while len(out) < total:
            pick = rng.random()
            remaining = total - len(out)
            if pick < 0.2:
                chunk = _rand_bytes(rng, min(remaining, rng.randint(1, 256)))
            elif pick < 0.4:
                chunk = _pattern_incrementing(min(remaining, rng.randint(16, 512)))
            elif pick < 0.6:
                chunk = _pattern_repeat(b"\x00", min(remaining, rng.randint(16, 512)))
            elif pick < 0.8:
                chunk = _pattern_repeat(b"\xFF", min(remaining, rng.randint(16, 512)))
            else:
                chunk = _pattern_repeat(b"ABCDEF\x00\xFF", min(remaining, rng.randint(16, 512)))
            out.extend(chunk)
        return bytes(out)

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Generator for "text string (unspecified encoding)" inputs used by many stubs via FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME
# Goals:
# - Produce a NUL-terminated textual buffer containing interesting path-like and general strings
# - Include valid UTF-8 cases, common filesystem edge cases, and random bytes
# - Stay within 4096 bytes
# - Deterministic given seed but varied per call
#
# The fuzz stubs consume FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME. Many functions expect NUL-terminated C strings
# and sometimes path semantics. We'll emit a single bytes blob that contains multiple concatenated strings separated
# by NULs so the harness can carve strings as needed.
#
# Strategy:
# - Build a catalog of strings:
#   * Typical filenames and directories
#   * Absolute/relative paths, with/without trailing slashes
#   * Wildcards, unicode names, long names
#   * Password-like strings
#   * Empty and very short strings
#   * Encoded edge sequences (dot files, spaces, quoting, windows paths)
#   * Random-length random bytes interpreted as text
# - Randomly select and synthesize variants, including platform separators / and \
# - Ensure each entry is NUL-terminated; final buffer is concatenation of entries
#
# Consumers:
# - mz_os_utf8_string_create(in.c_str(), encoding) => needs arbitrary bytes
# - Various mz_zip_* functions use filenames/comments/passwords
# - mz_stream_*_open accept paths and arbitrary strings
#
# We do not perform file I/O; FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME is handled by fuzzer framework. We just provide rich strings.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

def _rand_bytes(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _utf8_samples() -> List[str]:
    return [
        "",  # empty
        ".", "..",
        "a", "A", "0",
        "file.txt", "readme.MD", "archive.zip", "data.bin",
        "space name.txt", "tabs\tinside", "newline\ninside",
        "..\\weird\\path", "..//mix/sep\\arators",
        "./relative/path/", "../up/one/level/",
        "/absolute/unix/path", "/", "//network/share",  # UNC-like start
        "C:/Windows/System32", "C:\\Windows\\System32", "C:",
        "tmp", "/tmp", "var/log/system.log",
        "*.txt", "?.zip", "[a-z]*.c",
        "con", "nul", "prn",  # Windows reserved
        "aux.txt", "com1", "lpt9",
        "trailingslash/", "noslash",
        "dots.end.", ".hidden", "...",
        "name.with.many.dots.ext",
        "verylong" + "_name" * 50 + ".bin",
        # Unicode samples
        "üñïçødé.txt", "日本語/ファイル.txt", "emoji_😀.txt", "Россия/данные.zip",
        "العربية/ملف.txt", "हिन्दी/फ़ाइल.txt", "한국어/파일.txt",
        # Symlink-like
        "link -> target", "././/double//slashes//",
        # Trailing spaces and dots (Windows edge)
        "trailing_space ", "trailing_dot.",
        # Relative special components
        "./", "../", "../../deep/path",
    ]

def _password_samples() -> List[str]:
    return [
        "password", "", "123456", "letmein", "correct horse battery staple",
        "p@$$w0rd!", "🔒secret🔑", "null\x00byte?", "long" * 32,
    ]

def _comment_samples() -> List[str]:
    return [
        "", "Created by minizip-ng", "测试注释", "with newlines\nsecond line",
        "a" * 255, "b" * 1023,
    ]

def _join_path(parts: List[str], sep: str) -> str:
    # Normalize joins a bit: avoid double sep unless explicitly present
    out = []
    for i, p in enumerate(parts):
        if i == 0:
            out.append(p.rstrip("/\\"))
        else:
            out.append(p.strip("/\\"))
    s = sep.join(out)
    return s

def _gen_paths(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    seps = ["/", "\\"]
    bases = ["/tmp", "/var/log", "/home/user", "C:/Temp", "C:/Users/Public", ".", "..", "./build"]
    names = [
        "a.txt", "b", "dir", "deep", "nested", "file.tar.gz", "NUL", "COM1",
        "复杂", "😀", "spaces here", "mix.ed.chars", "data" + str(r.randrange(1000))
    ]
    out = []
    for _ in range(24):
        sep = r.choice(seps)
        depth = r.randrange(1, 6)
        parts = [r.choice(bases)] + [r.choice(names) for _ in range(depth)]
        s = _join_path(parts, sep)
        # randomly add trailing slash
        if r.random() < 0.4:
            s += sep
        out.append(s)
    return out

def _rand_utf8(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    # Generate random valid-ish UTF-8 by assembling code points with varying ranges
    length = r.randrange(min_len, max_len + 1)
    chars = []
    for _ in range(length):
        p = r.random()
        if p < 0.6:
            code = r.randrange(0x20, 0x7F)  # printable ASCII
        elif p < 0.75:
            code = r.randrange(0xA0, 0x07FF)  # 2-byte
        elif p < 0.9:
            code = r.randrange(0x0800, 0xD7FF)  # 3-byte excluding surrogates start
        else:
            # Skip surrogate range and U+FFFE/FFFF non-characters rarely
            code = r.randrange(0xE000, 0x10FFFF)
            if 0xFDD0 <= code <= 0xFDEF or (code & 0xFFFE) == 0xFFFE:
                code = 0xFFFD
        chars.append(chr(code))
    return "".join(chars)

def _make_entries(r: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    entries: List[bytes] = []

    # Core UTF-8/path samples
    for s in _utf8_samples():
        entries.append(s.encode('utf-8', errors='surrogatepass') + b"\x00")

    # Password/comment pools
    for s in _password_samples() + _comment_samples():
        entries.append(s.encode('utf-8', errors='surrogatepass') + b"\x00")

    # Synthesized paths
    for s in _gen_paths(r):
        entries.append(s.encode('utf-8', errors='surrogatepass') + b"\x00")

    # Random UTF-8 blobs
    for _ in range(10):
        s = _rand_utf8(r, 0, 64)
        entries.append(s.encode('utf-8', errors='surrogatepass') + b"\x00")

    # Pure random bytes segments (not guaranteed valid UTF-8) to exercise arbitrary encodings
    for _ in range(6):
        n = r.randrange(0, 128)
        b = _rand_bytes(r, n)
        # Ensure no interior NUL truncation surprise? It's acceptable; many callers accept arbitrary bytes
        entries.append(b + b"\x00")

    # Specific edge: extremely long filename within reasonable bound
    long_name = ("L" * 4000) + ".txt"
    entries.append(long_name.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00")

    return entries

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Produce a shuffled selection of entries and pack until MAX_TOTAL
    entries = _make_entries(r)
    r.shuffle(entries)

    buf = bytearray()
    for e in entries:
        if len(buf) + len(e) > MAX_TOTAL:
            # Always ensure we end with a NUL terminator boundary
            if not buf or buf[-1] != 0:
                buf.append(0)
            break
        buf.extend(e)

    # If buffer ended up empty, add a minimal NUL string
    if not buf:
        buf.extend(b"\x00")

    # Guarantee final NUL terminator
    if buf[-1] != 0:
        buf.append(0)

    return bytes(buf)
